title: JR Kyushu Estimates Kumamoto Earthquake Impact at ¥17 Billion; Interim Profit Falls for Third Straight Year
text:
JR Kyushu Estimates Kumamoto Earthquake Impact at ¥17 Billion; Interim Profit Falls for Third Straight Year — BigGo Finance Ask AI Real-time News Market Earnings Call Event Calendar Watchlist Podcast Market Influencers Earnings Call Event Calendar Watchlist Podcast Market Influencers More Ask AI Real-time News Watchlist Holdings Market Earnings Call Event Calendar Podcast Market Influencers JR Kyushu Estimates Kumamoto Earthquake Impact at ¥17 Billion; Interim Profit Falls for Third Straight Year
 Add preferred source JR Kyushu announced that the impact of the July Kumamoto Earthquake is expected to total approximately ¥17 billion (about $107.2 million). The estimate includes roughly ¥9 billion (about $56.8 million) to restore elevated bridges and other infrastructure on the Kyushu Shinkansen, about ¥6.7 billion (about $42.3 million) in lost railway passenger transport revenue from partial service suspensions, and about ¥400 million (about $2.5 million) for substitute bus transportation. Net profit for the fiscal 2026 interim consolidated results fell 3.8% year-on-year to ¥21.4 billion (about $135.0 million), marking a third consecutive year of profit decline, and the company cut its full-year net profit forecast for the fiscal year ending March 2027 to ¥47 billion (about $296.5 million) from ¥51.6 billion (about $325.5 million). President Yoji Furumiya noted the significant management impact of the Shinkansen damage and said the full restoration costs have not yet been finalized. Key Elements 
 JR Kyushu Yoji Furumiya Kumamoto Earthquake Kyushu Shinkansen Kagoshima Line railway passenger transport revenue JR Kyushu said on the 4th that the impact of the Kumamoto Earthquake that struck in July on its business results is expected to total approximately ¥17 billion (about $107.2 million). The breakdown consists of about ¥9 billion (about $56.8 million) for restoring railway facilities, about ¥6.7 billion (about $42.3 million) in lost railway passenger transport revenue due to partial suspensions of the Kyushu Shinkansen and other factors, and about ¥400 million (about $2.5 million) for substitute bus transportation. In the fiscal 2026 interim consolidated results announced the same day, net profit fell 3.8% year-on-year to ¥21.4 billion (about $135.0 million), recording a third consecutive year of profit decline.
 The restoration costs mainly comprise about ¥7 billion (about $44.2 million) in damage to elevated bridges and other structures on the Kyushu Shinkansen, and about ¥1.9 billion (about $12.0 million) in damage to rails and utility poles on the Kagoshima Line and to Shinkansen trains. Most of the revenue decline stemmed from partial suspensions of the Kyushu Shinkansen, which lasted nearly two months. Railway passenger transport revenue also fell for the first time in six years, weighing on profit.
 The company also revised down its consolidated earnings forecast for the fiscal year ending March 2027, cutting its net profit projection by ¥4.6 billion (about $29.0 million) to ¥47 billion (about $296.5 million) from the previously forecast ¥51.6 billion (about $325.5 million). It will record about ¥9 billion (about $56.8 million) in damage to railway facilities from the Kumamoto Earthquake as an extraordinary loss. The sales forecast was left unchanged.
 President Yoji Furumiya, speaking at a press conference, said, "This time I was made to feel that when the Shinkansen is damaged, it has an extremely large impact on management," explaining that the damage to elevated bridges was substantial. He added, "The Shinkansen is still at the temporary restoration stage, so how much full restoration will cost has not yet been finalized."
 Item Amount (estimate) 
 Railway facility restoration costs approx. ¥9 billion 
 — of which Kyushu Shinkansen elevated bridges, etc. approx. ¥7 billion 
 — of which Kagoshima Line and train damage approx. ¥1.9 billion 
 Decline in railway passenger transport revenue approx. ¥6.7 billion 
 Substitute bus transportation costs approx. ¥400 million 
 Total impact approx. ¥17 billion 
 Note: All amounts are estimates based on JR Kyushu's announcements. The breakdown of restoration costs lists only the main items.
 Earnings item Fiscal 2026 interim Year-on-year 
 Net profit ¥21.4 billion down 3.8% 
 Fiscal year ending March 2027 net profit forecast ¥47 billion (previously ¥51.6 billion) cut by ¥4.6 billion 
 The Kyushu Shinkansen suspensions also cast a shadow over efforts to capture tourism demand. JR Kyushu said railway passenger transport revenue fell for the first time in six years, and capacity constraints may persist until full restoration gets underway. The company says the costs required for full restoration have not been finalized at this point, leaving a risk of additional cost provisions going forward.
